title: Archipelago Data — On-prem quantization deployment & upgrade playbook (draft)
content:
Context:
Archipelago Data (customer) — pilot private deployment for sensitive genomics preprocessing workloads. Primary requirement: on-prem VPC deployment with deterministic latency for model scoring pipelines, optional HSM-backed KMS for key management, and aggressive model quantization to reduce VRAM and unit cost. This doc captures the on-prem sizing recommendation, terraform module notes for the cutover/upgrade, operational runbook, risk/rollback plan, and open Q&A items.

Status summary (short):
- Current: prototype cluster (4x A100-40GB nodes) running inference from model-v1. Team completed functional tests but needs production-grade rollout plan.
- Goal: move to quantized model-pair (fp16 for quality-critical routes, q4_0/q5_0 where acceptable) on an HA k8s cluster with predictable autoscale and KMS integration.
- Timeline target: phased canary -> full cutover within 6 weeks from approval.

Assumptions (customer + infra):
- Customer network: private datacenter with internal BGP and VLAN segmentation. We assume egress to Redwood control-plane (optional) over TLS allowed on 443 and 5222 (for metrics ingestion). Confirmed? ACTION: customer networking team.
- Storage: NFS v4.1 available for model artifacts and shard cache (latency-sensitive). If not, recommend Ceph/Rook.
- KMS: customer will provide an HSM-backed KMS with PKCS11 endpoint for server-side key signing and envelope encryption.
- Cluster orchestration: k8s 1.26 (kubeadm) preferred. If customer uses older version, we will provide compatibility shim.
- Terraform state storage: remote S3-compatible bucket with versioning + Dynamo/consul locking.
- Model sizes: main model ~16B parameters; quantized footprint expected: ~20–24 GB VRAM with q4_0; fp16 ~32–36 GB.
- Target latency SLO: 95th-percentile < 75ms for single-turn scoring under steady traffic (small prompt).

High-level sizing recommendation (production):
- Inference nodes: 6 nodes with 80 GB GPU equivalent (e.g., 4x H100-80GB split or physical HW that provides similar aggregate). If H100 unavailable, use 8x A40/A10G depending on cosine-cost tradeoffs.
- Control/infra nodes: 3x m5.large equivalent for k8s control plane (HA).
- Autoscaling policy: min=4 GPUs active (to satisfy baseline throughput), scale step +2 GPUs, cooldown 5m.
- Prefill cache size: allocate 128GB host RAM per node for KV/prefix caches; adjust after load test.
- Disk: 2TB NVMe per node for model shards and swap in case of reloading.

Terraform module notes (modules to use / change):
- Module names: ri_vpc_private, ri_onprem_k8s_cluster, ri_tf_kms_connector, ri_gpu_node_pool, ri_monitoring_agent.
- Recommended module bumps: move ri_onprem_k8s_cluster from v0.9.1 -> v1.2.0 (adds kubelet flags for hugepages & device plugin). Review breaking changes: removed legacy nodepool resource; must migrate states.
- State migration plan:
  - Step 1: snapshot remote state and create a migration branch.
  - Step 2: use `terraform state mv` to rename legacy module resources to new module path (document exact paths in runbook).
  - Step 3: plan/apply in staging with `-target=module.ri_onprem_k8s_cluster` to validate.
- Important providers: kubernetes provider pinned to 2.18.x, helm provider 2.7.x. New versions require kubeconfig v1.26 compatibility.
- Secrets: do NOT store KMS credentials in tfvars; use dynamic retrieval via `external` data source or Vault integration.

Quantization & model variant rollout plan:
- Two-track model deployment:
  - Track A (gold): fp16 model serving on dedicated pool for high-precision routes (billing-sensitive).
  - Track B (economy): q4_0/q5_0 quantized model on mixed pool for bulk background scoring.
- Canary strategy:
  - Canary 0 (internal): 5% traffic to q4 model using synthetic tests and golden prompts. Run A/B quality regression; log perplexity and specific eval sets.
  - Canary 1 (shadow): run q4 in shadow mode for 24–48h with real traffic, compare latencies and error rates.
  - Canary 2 (live canary): route 10% live traffic after gating on quality metrics.
- Quality gates: automated eval suite must show <=0.8% deviation on prioritized prompt set and no high-severity hallucination regressions.

Deployment steps (detailed):
1) Preflight (week -2 to -1):
   - Confirm network endpoints, NTP sync, and baselines.
   - Performance baseline: run current fp16 model under 0.5RPS/user profile; capture 95/99 latency and p95 token costs.
   - Verify KMS connectivity and test envelope encryption workflow.
   - Terraform: test apply in staging using new modules.
2) Canary phase (week 0–1):
   - Create dedicated k8s node pool `ri-quant-pool` with taints: `role=quant:NoSchedule` and label `ri/pool=economy`.
   - Deploy q4 model container with lowered prefetch and dynamic batching disabled for first 24h.
   - Observe memory pressure, OOM kills; tune kv-cache and per-request token limits.
3) Gradual scale (week 2–3):
   - Increase request share to 25% after passing quality gates. Enable batching with small window (10ms) to recover throughput.
4) Full cutover (week 4–6):
   - Migrate routing policy in control-plane to allow up to 60% economy traffic for non-critical routes.
   - Decommission test fp16 nodes only after stable metrics for 72h.

Rollback plan (if canary fails):
- Immediate: revert routing weights at the Redwood control-plane (instant TCP-level fallback).
- If tf apply changed k8s node pools: run `terraform apply` to restore previous module configuration (we keep previous node pool module in tfvars backup).
- If model process crashed due to quantized kernel bug: taint the quant pool node group and fallback to fp16 pool by changing serviceSelector.

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- View pods on quant pool: `kubectl get pods -l ri/pool=economy -o wide`
- Drain node: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- Force re-deploy model: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ri-model-quant --namespace=redwood`
- Terraform state snapshot: `terraform state pull > state-YYYYMMDD.json`

Open architecture Q&A (items for customer):
Q: Will Archipelago accept the recommended external metrics endpoint to send anonymized telemetry to Redwood?
A: Customer legal TBD; default assumption: metrics allowed, but PI removed and sample rate limited to 0.1%.

Q: HSM/KMS performance SLA — key signing latency requirement?
A: We need <10ms envelope decrypt for synchronous scoring. If not achievable, we must fallback to local ephemeral keys with HSM sealing.

Q: Are there strict maintenance windows for rolling kernel/driver upgrades?
A: Customer requires daytime windows only (08:00–20:00 local). Plan to schedule disruptive driver updates in off-peak 02:00–06:00 and get explicit signoff.

Risk register (top 6):
- Risk: Quantization introduces subtle token-level regressions that only show at scale. Mitigation: extended shadow runs + automated evals.
- Risk: Terraform module state migration causes accidental node replacement. Mitigation: snapshot state + manual `state mv` with dry-run.
- Risk: KMS latency > threshold. Mitigation: local caching layer + ephemeral keys.
- Risk: Network egress blocked. Mitigation: offline signing mode + customer whitelist steps.
- Risk: GPU driver mismatch. Mitigation: standardize driver image and test on staging with exact kernel.
- Risk: Unexpected memory pressure from KV cache. Mitigation: memory limits, OOM daemon alert.

Notes for SRE/Platform handoff:
- Provide prebuilt model images in private registry (tagging: `archipelago/model:quant-YYYYMMDD`).
- Include liveness/readiness endpoints that expose tokenization size and KV cache hit rate.
- Export Prometheus metrics: `ri_inference_latency_seconds`, `ri_kv_cache_hit_ratio`, `ri_model_load_time_seconds`.

Outstanding TODOs (short):

- [ ] Network egress allowance confirmation (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Finalize terraform migration steps and approve plan (owner: Maya).

Attachments & references:
- Terraform migration checklist (linked_artifacts: github PR + Confluence),
- Eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/archipelago-eval-sets,
- Driver/OS matrix: Confluence table (see linked_artifacts).

Appendix — quick module checklist (commands to run during maintenance window):
1) `git checkout -b deploy/archipelago/quant-upgrade`
2) `terraform init -upgrade`
3) `terraform plan -out tfplan.quant`
4) `terraform apply tfplan.quant` (targeted first to ri_onprem_k8s_cluster module)
5) run smoke tests (scripts/smoke/archipelago_smoke.sh)
6) promote to canary routing policy via control-plane UI or CLI (documented in step-runbook).

End of draft.

Author notes: this doc is intentionally prescriptive to speed decisioning. Expect iteration after customer answers the Q&A.
